messages.subject: Sampler worked in nimble version 0.10.1, but not in 0.11.1 or later
parts:
Hello,

I have a latent individual ID spatial capture-recapture sampler that worked fine in version 0.10.1, but when sending it to someone else today, I found out it does not work in versions  0.11.1 or later. I get no error messages, but I've narrowed down the problem. First, here is the BUGS code:

NimModel <- nimbleCode({
  #--------------------------------------------------------------
  # priors
  #--------------------------------------------------------------
  psi~dunif(0,1)
  p~dunif(0,1)
  sigma~dunif(0,100)
 
  #ID cov priors. If you change these distributions, need to change custom samplers. Used for conjugate custom sampler.
  for(m in 1:n.cov){
    #Distribution for G across individuals
    G.mu[m]~dnorm(0,sd=100)
    G.tau[m] ~ dgamma(0.001,0.001)
    G.sigma[m] <- sqrt(1/G.tau[m])
    #Distribution for G measurement error
    tau.obs[m] ~ dgamma(0.001,0.001)
    sigma.obs[m] <- sqrt(1/tau.obs[m])
  }
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------
  #likelihoods (except for s priors)
  #--------------------------------------------------------------
  for(i in 1:M){
    z[i] ~ dbern(psi)
    for(m in 1:n.cov){
      G.true[i,m]~dnorm(mean=G.mu[m],tau=G.tau[m])
    }
    s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim.s[1],xlim.s[2])
    s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim.s[1],ylim.s[2])
    
    for(k in 1:K){
      u[i,k,1]~dnorm(s[i,1],sd=sigma)
      u[i,k,2]~dnorm(s[i,2],sd=sigma)
      available[i,k] <- inout(u[i,k,1:2],xlim.p[1:2],ylim.p[1:2])
      y.true[i,k]~dbern(p*z[i]*available[i,k])
    }
  }
  #feature observation process
  for(l in 1:n.samples){
    for(m in 1:n.cov){
      G.obs[l,m,1:n.rep] ~ dnorm2(mu=G.true[ID[l],m],tau=tau.obs[m],n.rep = n.rep,na.ind=G.obs.NA.indicator[l,m,1:n.rep]) #custom distribution to skip missing values
    }
  }
  capcounts[1:M] <- Getcapcounts(y.true=y.true[1:M,1:K])
  n <- Getncap(capcounts=capcounts[1:M],ID=ID[1:n.samples],G.latent=G.latent[1:M,1:n.cov])
  N <- sum(z[1:M])
})# end model

In this model, y.true is the individual by occasion binary capture data. We don't observe ID directly, but we observe some "feature scores" in G.obs, which correlate with individual ID. So y.true needs to be updated on each iteration. I have a custom sampler to do this and it worked in version 0.10.1.

In version 0.10.1, Nimble will assign a posterior predictive update for y.true, which is incorrect, and I replaced it with an update that is correct. Since I don't have 0.10.1 installed, the following are the samplers assigned except for y.true:

===== Monitors =====
thin = 1: G.mu, G.sigma, n, N, p, psi, sigma, sigma.obs
thin2 = 1: ID, u
===== Samplers =====
RW sampler (3380)
  - psi
  - p
  -sigma
  - tau.obs[]  (3 elements)
  - s[]  (450 elements)
  - G.true[]  (675 elements)
  - u[]  (2250 elements)
conjugate sampler (6)
  - G.mu[]  (3 elements)
  - G.tau[]  (3 elements)
binary sampler (225)
  - z[]  (225 elements)

We see we get random walk updates for psi, p, and sigma. As previously stated, nimble will list a posterior predictive update for y.true, and I replaced it.

In version 0.11.1, nimble does not list a sampler assigned to y.true, but it updates it anyway. When I try to replace the sampler for y.true with my custom sampler and then printSamplers('y.true'), it lists my custom sampler there. But the results are nonsense. I'm 99% sure Nimble is doing both the posterior predicitve update and my custom update because the constraints I impose in the custom update are not maintained.

A final observation is that the code works fine if I treat y.true as completely known.

So in summary, I think nimble is assigning a sampler to y.true, but not listing it wherever printSamplers pulls from, and so it can't be removed. But it is still used. Does this sound correct?

parts:
One more clue. This issue is also affecting another, similar sampler for SCR with unknown left and right flank linkages. Relevant latent data lines are in red below:

NimModel <- nimbleCode({
  #detection function priors
  p0B~dunif(0,1)
  #if you do not want to share p0L and p0R
  # p0L~dunif(0,1)
  # p0R~dunif(0,1)
  # #if you want to share p0L and p0R
  p0S ~ dunif(0,1)
  p0L <- p0S
  p0R <- p0S
  #Make sure upper bound on sigma uniform prior is appropriate
  sigma~dunif(0,20)
  #data augmentation prior
  psi~dunif(0,1)
#likelihoods (except for s priors)

for(i in 1:M) {
    z[i] ~ dbern(psi)

s[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1],xlim[2])
    s[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1],ylim[2])
    d2[i,1:J] <- GetD2(s = s[i,1:2], X = X[1:J,1:2],z=z[i])
    pd.B[i,1:J] <- GetDetectionProb(p0=p0B,sigma=sigma,d2=d2[i,1:J],z=z[i])
    pd.L[i,1:J] <- GetDetectionProb(p0=p0L,sigma=sigma,d2=d2[i,1:J],z=z[i])
    pd.R[i,1:J] <- GetDetectionProb(p0=p0R,sigma=sigma,d2=d2[i,1:J],z=z[i])
    y.B.true[i,1:J,1:K] ~ dBernoulliVectorBoth(pd.B[i,1:J],K2D=K2D[1:J,1:K],z=z[i])
    y.L.true[i,1:J,1:K] ~ dBernoulliVectorSingle(pd.L[i,1:J],K2D=K2D[1:J,1:K],z=z[i])
    y.R.true[i,1:J,1:K] ~ dBernoulliVectorSingle(pd.R[i,1:J],K2D=K2D[1:J,1:K],z=z[i])
  }
  #have to trick Nimble to know ID is part of model by using it somewhere in model statement
  IDdummy <- IDdummyfun(ID.L=ID.L[1:n.L],ID.R=ID.R[1:n.R])

N <- sum(z[1:M])
})# end model

In this case, nimble is not assigning any sampler to y.L.true and y.R.true, but it assigns a posterior predictive branch sampler to p0S, which depends on these two data structures. If I replace this posterior predictive branch sampler for p0S, it works fine. But obviously, it does not work otherwise.

This seems to be a slightly different issue. I'm not sure why nimble supplied an incorrect latent ID update in the first sampler I posted about, but not this one. I supply arrays completely filled with NA's for the data for y.L.true and y.R.true as I do in the previous sampler. Regardless, these issues probably relate to the addition of the posterior predictive branch sampler.

Ben

Ben, let me explain briefly about the (newly introduced) posterior predictive branch sampler (hereafter: "branch sampler"), and what I'm seeing from your model.

The branch sampler was introduced in nimble version 0.11.1, to jointly sample trailing branches of the model which contain no data whatsoever.  These branches are thus jointly-posterior-predictive.  That is, say there's a model with node x, and y depends on x, and z depends on y, but *none* of x, y, or z are data (information flows as x -> y -> z, or if arrows denote dependence upon, then x <- y <- z).  Then, instead of (previous nimble behaviour) assigning RW or perhaps conjugate samplers to x and y, and a posterior predictive sampler to z, it would make sense to jointly sample (x,y,z) by calling the simulate methods (in order) of each of these nodes.  Since none of them are data, we can simulate x (conditional on everything "upwards" in the model that x depends on), then simulate y (conditional on the new value of x), and finally simulate z (conditional on the new value of y).  That's essentially how the branch sampler operates.  (Noting, and we've seen one case of this before, where user-defined distributions which may/may not have a simulation function ("r"-distribution), the branch sampler might not play nicely in this instance, and that's something that might need attention).

Also worth noting, for the model structure above, the old nimble behaviour would assign (and print) samplers along the lines of:
RW samplers: x and y
posterior predictive sampler: z
Clearly showing how nimble plans on updating each of x, y, and z.

The new nimble behaviour, using the new branch sampler, which perhaps could be improved, now only shows:
branch sampler: x
And it's left somewhat unclear to understand that internal to this branch sampler on x is sampling the whole branch following from entirely-non-data branch point (x), and everything downstream of it (y, z) internal to the sampler.  So, point being, in printing the samplers you wouldn't actually see anything "assigned' to sample y or z.

Looking into your model, at least from your first two emails, was a little difficult since I couldn't create the model (missing the constants and data, in particular), and also I"m missing the custom functions and distributions you're using (of which there are several).

That said, I tried to study the dependence structure carefully, and also gleaned a few clues from your print-outs of the sampler assignments (from versions 0.10 and 0.11).  Critically, understanding the dependency structure is important for thinking about the branch sampler.

As best I can tell from looking at this output, it seems like the model has two *disjoint* graphs:
psi, p, sigma, s, z, u, available, y.true
If (as I suspect) *none* of these quantities are specified as data (excluding "available" which is deterministic), then here's what you're seeing for this first disjoint graph:
Nothing is data.
Every "top" node is a branch point for exclusively non-data dependencies (those being: psi, p, sigma, s)
Therefore, a branch sampler is assigned to each of: psi, p, sigma, s - exactly what you're seeing, under version 0.11, per your 4th email.

There's another (entirely disjoint) graph in your model:
G.mu, G.tau, G.true, tau.obs, G.obs
The dependence structure culminates in G.obs; and no samplers are ever assigned to G.obs, so I infer G.obs is assigned as data.  Since these nodes (G.mu, G.tau, G.true, tau.obs) all have trailing data beneath them in the dependency structure (that being: G.obs), there are no branch nor posterior predictive samplers assigned in this 2nd disjoint graph, and other samplers are assigned (e.g., RW, conjugate), and operate as you'd expect on G.mu, G.tau, tau.obs, etc.

I will not claim to fully understand your model, but I'm suspicious about these two *entirely disjoint* graphs making up your model.  Is it possible there's intended to be some sort of dependence upon the 1st graph (including, perhaps, y.true) existing in the 2nd graph (perhaps in the, data G.obs)?  If so, then the data G.obs would actually influence estimation of top parameters such as psi, p, sigma, etc.  This dependence in G.obs could be manifested as dependence on any of the quantities derived from y.true, as well, for example capcounts, or quite simply "n", being used anywhere in the 2nd graph.

Anyway, as it stands: you're seeing branch samplers assigned to psi, p, sigma, and s, because they have no data depending on them in the graphical structure.  Internal to each of these branch samplers, for example that assigned to sigma, nimble calls the simulate methods of (sigma, u, available (which is a deterministic calculation of the value), and y.true).  And this also explains your observation about no sampler being assigned to "z", because the branch sampler assigned to psi, internally, calls the simulation methods of (psi, z, y.true).

I also recognize the possibility that this missing "dependency" between the graphs actually exists in the custom sampler you've written, and that you're assigning to y.true.  That's an advanced use of the system, and could be perfectly valid, but the default sampler assignments certainly would not detect that.  Please let me know if that's the case, which would be something else to think about.

I also admit, I did not study the other model ("similar sampler for SCR with unknown left and right flank linkages") from your 3rd email.  I'm hoping I've explained enough about the branch sampler, that your questions about that model will now make sense.

Anyway, this was long-winded, but I tried to explain about the new branch sampler, and explain some of your (and my) observations about your model and the sampler assignments.  Please take your time reading through this and parsing it, and hopefully it makes sense.

If you still have other questions, don't hesitate to follow up further.

Cheers,
Daniel

Nothing is data.
Every "top" node is a branch point for exclusively non-data dependencies (those being: psi, p, sigma, s)

On Tue, Oct 26, 2021 at 9:31 PM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
Ben, let me explain briefly about the (newly introduced) posterior predictive branch sampler (hereafter: "branch sampler"), and what I'm seeing from your model.

The branch sampler was introduced in nimble version 0.11.1, to jointly sample trailing branches of the model which contain no data whatsoever.  These branches are thus jointly-posterior-predictive.  That is, say there's a model with node x, and y depends on x, and z depends on y, but *none* of x, y, or z are data (information flows as x -> y -> z, or if arrows denote dependence upon, then x <- y <- z).  Then, instead of (previous nimble behaviour) assigning RW or perhaps conjugate samplers to x and y, and a posterior predictive sampler to z, it would make sense to jointly sample (x,y,z) by calling the simulate methods (in order) of each of these nodes.  Since none of them are data, we can simulate x (conditional on everything "upwards" in the model that x depends on), then simulate y (conditional on the new value of x), and finally simulate z (conditional on the new value of y).  That's essentially how the branch sampler operates.  (Noting, and we've seen one case of this before, where user-defined distributions which may/may not have a simulation function ("r"-distribution), the branch sampler might not play nicely in this instance, and that's something that might need attention).

Also worth noting, for the model structure above, the old nimble behaviour would assign (and print) samplers along the lines of:
RW samplers: x and y
posterior predictive sampler: z
Clearly showing how nimble plans on updating each of x, y, and z.

The new nimble behaviour, using the new branch sampler, which perhaps could be improved, now only shows:
branch sampler: x
And it's left somewhat unclear to understand that internal to this branch sampler on x is sampling the whole branch following from entirely-non-data branch point (x), and everything downstream of it (y, z) internal to the sampler.  So, point being, in printing the samplers you wouldn't actually see anything "assigned' to sample y or z.

Looking into your model, at least from your first two emails, was a little difficult since I couldn't create the model (missing the constants and data, in particular), and also I"m missing the custom functions and distributions you're using (of which there are several).

That said, I tried to study the dependence structure carefully, and also gleaned a few clues from your print-outs of the sampler assignments (from versions 0.10 and 0.11).  Critically, understanding the dependency structure is important for thinking about the branch sampler.

As best I can tell from looking at this output, it seems like the model has two *disjoint* graphs:
psi, p, sigma, s, z, u, available, y.true
If (as I suspect) *none* of these quantities are specified as data (excluding "available" which is deterministic), then here's what you're seeing for this first disjoint graph:
Nothing is data.
Every "top" node is a branch point for exclusively non-data dependencies (those being: psi, p, sigma, s)
Therefore, a branch sampler is assigned to each of: psi, p, sigma, s - exactly what you're seeing, under version 0.11, per your 4th email.

There's another (entirely disjoint) graph in your model:
G.mu, G.tau, G.true, tau.obs, G.obs
The dependence structure culminates in G.obs; and no samplers are ever assigned to G.obs, so I infer G.obs is assigned as data.  Since these nodes (G.mu, G.tau, G.true, tau.obs) all have trailing data beneath them in the dependency structure (that being: G.obs), there are no branch nor posterior predictive samplers assigned in this 2nd disjoint graph, and other samplers are assigned (e.g., RW, conjugate), and operate as you'd expect on G.mu, G.tau, tau.obs, etc.

I will not claim to fully understand your model, but I'm suspicious about these two *entirely disjoint* graphs making up your model.  Is it possible there's intended to be some sort of dependence upon the 1st graph (including, perhaps, y.true) existing in the 2nd graph (perhaps in the, data G.obs)?  If so, then the data G.obs would actually influence estimation of top parameters such as psi, p, sigma, etc.  This dependence in G.obs could be manifested as dependence on any of the quantities derived from y.true, as well, for example capcounts, or quite simply "n", being used anywhere in the 2nd graph.

Anyway, as it stands: you're seeing branch samplers assigned to psi, p, sigma, and s, because they have no data depending on them in the graphical structure.  Internal to each of these branch samplers, for example that assigned to sigma, nimble calls the simulate methods of (sigma, u, available (which is a deterministic calculation of the value), and y.true).  And this also explains your observation about no sampler being assigned to "z", because the branch sampler assigned to psi, internally, calls the simulation methods of (psi, z, y.true).

I also recognize the possibility that this missing "dependency" between the graphs actually exists in the custom sampler you've written, and that you're assigning to y.true.  That's an advanced use of the system, and could be perfectly valid, but the default sampler assignments certainly would not detect that.  Please let me know if that's the case, which would be something else to think about.

I also admit, I did not study the other model ("similar sampler for SCR with unknown left and right flank linkages") from your 3rd email.  I'm hoping I've explained enough about the branch sampler, that your questions about that model will now make sense.

Anyway, this was long-winded, but I tried to explain about the new branch sampler, and explain some of your (and my) observations about your model and the sampler assignments.  Please take your time reading through this and parsing it, and hopefully it makes sense.

If you still have other questions, don't hesitate to follow up further.

Cheers,
Daniel

Nothing is data.
